newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador starts criminal proceedings against Bucaram.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador starts criminal proceedings against Bucaram.

text.p: Ecuador's supreme court on Friday initiated criminal proceedings against deposed President Abdala Bucaram on corruption charges.

The proceedings were started "considering that during the government of former President Abdala Bucaram there have been acts of corruption with public funds," a legal report signed by Carlos Sororzano, the president of the supreme court, said.

The report included arrest orders for Oscar Celleri, Bucaram's former private secretary, Miguel Salem, the former administration general secretary and Enrique Villon, the presidential head of finance.
"The government supports absolutely (the decision by the court). (As president) I have to respect the decisions of the supreme court," President Fabian Alarcon told journalists.
There was no arrest order for Bucaram, who moved to Panama after he was dismissed by Congress in February on grounds of "mental incompetence."

Alarcon would not say whether the government would have Bucaram extradited from Panama. "I have to analyse it. At this moment I do not have all the details (on the process of extradition), but everything which is within the law we support," he said.
The proceedings against Bucaram were initiated after Gustavo Teran, a deputy for the Popular Democratic Movement, accused Bucaram of irregularities in the management of presidential expenses.

According to the current government, which took over after Bucaram was deposed, the former president misappropriated $76 million during his six months in government. Some of that money, the government says, was used to buy the votes of seven deputies, each of whom received $1.5 million.
